description: Compact fact-pattern fixtures for the remaining five template types. Each type gets at least one canonical scenario so the R5 validator regression catches a prompt tweak that accidentally drops a hard requirement. Extensible to 3/type once an operator grades the live-LLM output.

facts.children_details: One child, Aarav, 5 years old, in petitioner's custody.

facts.property_address: Flat 12A, Sunshine Apartments, Andheri West, Mumbai
facts.relief_sought: Remove the unauthorised partition erected on the common landing within fifteen days, failing which legal proceedings will follow.

statement_paragraphs: I am the counsel on record for the petitioner in WP No. 1234/2026.
The contents of the accompanying petition are true to my knowledge based on the records of the matter.
No facts material to the petition have been suppressed.

facts.narrative: Accused induced the complainant to invest INR 10,00,000 in a fictitious real-estate scheme. Accused forged the allotment letter and has since absconded.

facts.impugned_order_summary: The Sessions Court rejected the appellant's application for stay on the recovery proceedings, holding that no prima facie case for stay was made out and that the balance of convenience lay with the respondent revenue authority.
questions_of_law: Whether the Sessions Court erred in declining stay despite the demand exceeding the assessed liability by 38%.
Whether the balance of convenience requires deposit of the disputed component pending appeal.
facts.grounds_brief: 1. The Sessions Court overlooked the appellant's documented payment of the undisputed component of the demand. 2. The court mis-read Annexure D-2 (statutory acknowledgement). 3. The court applied the wrong test for stay under CPC Order XLI Rule 5 by demanding security for the entire demand rather than the disputed portion. 4. No reasoned finding was recorded on irreparable injury despite the appellant placing on record bank-statement evidence of liquidity strain.
facts.interim_relief_sought: Stay of recovery proceedings pending hearing of this appeal, conditional on deposit of the undisputed component already paid.
facts.record_references: Impugned order at pp. 14-19 of paper-book; Annexure D-2 at p. 47; bank statements at pp. 81-93.

facts.respondent_name: Union of India through Ministry of Personnel
facts.impugned_action: The respondent has failed to dispose of the petitioner's representation dated 2025-08-12 seeking sanction for prosecution under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, despite the statutory three-month timeline having expired.
prayer_clauses: Direct the respondent to dispose of the petitioner's representation dated 2025-08-12 within four weeks.
Pass any other order this Hon'ble Court deems fit.
facts.interim_relief_sought: Pending disposal, restrain the respondent from acting on any contrary administrative communication.
facts.laches_position: The petitioner has approached this Hon'ble Court promptly upon expiry of the statutory timeline.

facts.impugned_proceedings_summary: FIR registered under BNS s.318 (cheating) arising out of a commercial dispute over a stalled real-estate transaction. The parties have since entered into a written compromise dated 2026-02-10 under which the petitioner has refunded the disputed amount with interest.
facts.grounds_for_quashing: The dispute is predominantly civil and commercial in nature; the parties have entered into a written compromise; continuation of proceedings would be an abuse of the process of court.

preliminary_objections: The plaint is barred by limitation under Article 54 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
The suit is undervalued for the purpose of pecuniary jurisdiction.
facts.paragraph_wise_reply: Para 1 is a matter of record. Para 2 is admitted insofar as the agreement to sell dated 2024-05-01 is concerned. Para 3 is denied; the plaintiff failed to tender the balance consideration within the time stipulated. Para 4 is denied for want of knowledge. Paras 5 to 8 are denied save and except as specifically admitted herein.
facts.limitation_defence: The cause of action accrued on 2024-12-01 when the plaintiff defaulted; the suit filed on 2026-04-15 is beyond the three-year limitation period.
documents_relied: Bank statements showing non-receipt of balance consideration

facts.main_petition_summary: The petitioner challenges Notification No. 12/2025 dated 2025-11-30 on the ground that it violates Articles 14 and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution.
facts.paragraph_wise_response: The contents of paras 1 to 3 are matters of record. Para 4 is denied. The notification was issued after due consultation with the stakeholder ministries and an inter-ministerial review committee, and is a valid exercise of statutory power conferred under s.5 of the parent Act. Paras 5 and 6 are denied. The remaining paras are denied save to the extent expressly admitted.
additional_facts_pleaded: The respondent has placed on record the inter-ministerial consultation file by way of separate affidavit.
The petitioner has suppressed the fact that representations were entertained by the respondent on 2026-01-10 and 2026-02-15.
facts.preliminary_submissions: The writ petition is liable to be dismissed at the threshold for suppression of material facts and for want of cause of action.
facts.relief_sought_against_petition: Dismiss the writ petition with costs.

facts.grounds_for_quashing: The petitioner and the aggrieved person have arrived at a comprehensive settlement of their matrimonial disputes, including a mutually-acceptable visitation schedule for the minor child. Continuation of the magistrate proceedings would be an abuse of process and is no longer in the interest of either party or the child.

facts.arbitration_agreement_summary: Clause 18 of the Master Services Agreement dated 2024-04-01 provides for resolution of all disputes by a sole arbitrator under the Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996, with the seat at Mumbai.
interim_reliefs_sought: Restrain the respondent from invoking Bank Guarantee BG/2025/0142 dated 2025-08-10 pending resolution by the arbitral tribunal.
Direct the respondent to deposit INR 5,00,00,000 with the court as security for the disputed amount.
facts.underlying_cause_of_action: The respondent has issued a notice on 2026-04-20 invoking the bank guarantee on a fraudulent claim of breach. The applicant has performed all obligations under the contract and any encashment would cause irreparable injury.
facts.urgency_basis: Without immediate court intervention, the bank guarantee will be encashed within 7 days and the security would be irrevocably lost; the arbitral tribunal cannot be constituted in time.
facts.undertaking_offered: The applicant offers to keep the disputed amount of INR 5,00,00,000 in a fixed deposit with a nationalised bank pending the arbitration.

facts.proposed_amendments: Add para 14-A: 'The plaintiff has, after the filing of this suit, discovered Annexure P-12 (the original board resolution dated 2023-11-15) which establishes that the respondent's signatory was duly authorised to bind the respondent. Para 11 of the plaint stands amended to that extent.' Delete para 17 of the plaint.
facts.reason_for_amendment: Annexure P-12 was retained by the respondent and was produced for the first time during third-party discovery on 2026-03-10. Without this amendment, the plaint would not reflect the true position on authority.
facts.due_diligence_explanation: The plaintiff conducted document searches in 2024 and 2025 through its company secretary and external counsel, and the respondent did not produce Annexure P-12 until compelled discovery in March 2026. The plaintiff could not have discovered the document earlier despite due diligence.
facts.prejudice_to_opposite_party: The amendment narrows the issues and does not introduce a new cause of action; the respondent has already had the document in its possession since 2023 and has admitted authenticity in its discovery affidavit.

facts.settlement_terms: (i) The petitioner has paid the respondent INR 8,00,000 by way of full and final settlement of all monetary claims arising out of the underlying transaction, receipt acknowledged. (ii) The respondent withdraws all allegations made in the FIR and consents to quashing under BNSS s.528. (iii) The parties undertake not to initiate further proceedings against each other on the same cause of action.
